source: Logic Pro 12.3 User Guide, Apple, 'Drum Kit Designer mappings': the GM Standard column of the figure 'Drum Kit Designer GM Standard, GM + ModWheel, and Brush Snare keyboard mappings', in Logic's octave naming (C1 = 36). The octave reading agrees with notes measured from four Session Player drummer regions (36 Kick, 38 Snare Center, 40 Snare Rimshot, 42 Hi-Hat Closed, 34 Snare Edge).
note: name is the guide's label. term, duplicate_of and prefer are this table's choices, not Apple's, and so is every pairing with another map drawn from them. The map covers the GM Standard input mapping only: GM + ModWheel changes 42, 44 and 46 and moves hi-hat opening to the mod wheel, and brush snare kits add keys below 31, so neither is here. Toms are numbered by the GM keys they sit on (tom 4 low, tom 3 mid, tom 2 high) and a tom's edge extends its term; a tom 1, which the kit lacks, prefers the high tom. A crash's Stop is a choke and leads its term with that word, so no fallback reaches a strike.
